# Magik

> An opinionated, full-stack Ruby framework on TruffleRuby, and an **AI-first repository**: the primary developer is an AI agent, and every design decision follows from that. One uniform DSL grammar covers models, screens, actions, realtime channels, background jobs, ledgers, APIs and admin panels — a `ledger` is declared the way a `model` is, so there is one grammar to learn and one to hold in context. The server renders HTML and htmx handles interactivity; there is no SPA framework and never will be. Conventions are enforced at boot rather than documented: an unbalanced ledger, a `field :card_number`, a cross-domain reach, a screen holding state, a timestamp with no timezone, a surface reaching a model without naming an authorization verb — each is a boot failure carrying a stable `MAGIK_*` code, a one-sentence cause and a runnable `fix:` line, which is the correction signal an agent can act on without a human in the loop. Multi-tenant by default, UUIDv7 keys, integer-cents money, and a config-level swap behind every opinionated default. The CLI binary is `magik`. Install with `gem install magik`.

This file is a link map, not a status page. **It states no version, count or verdict without the command that resolves it** — a number written here goes stale on the next commit and the command does not. `As of 2026-08-26`.

**The one fact you must not get wrong:** `magik 0.0.1` is a **name reservation on RubyGems**. No framework code exists. Every DSL block in `wiki/` and `docs/` is a design artefact that has never been parsed. Three CLI commands run — `version`, `help` and `docs` — and everything else exits `1` with `MAGIK_CLI_COMMAND_NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. Resolve it with `magik help --json` before you quote anything else on this page.

## Which reader are you

Two different jobs, two different starting points. Pick one before reading further.

**A — You are implementing Magik.** You are writing framework code in this repository, landing a phase, adding a subsystem.

- [docs/idea/00-build-spec.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/00-build-spec.md) — the specification. The source of truth: amended from measurement, then rewritten as a clean v1. Nothing else contradicts it.
- [docs/idea/06-phases.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/06-phases.md) — the ten phases (1, 2, 3, 4, 4b, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) and the thirteen-step build order in detail, and what "done" means for each.
- [ROADMAP.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/ROADMAP.md) — the thirteen-step build order, the version milestones, and today's status.
- [docs/architecture/05-adding-a-feature.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/05-adding-a-feature.md) — the end-to-end loop with the exact command per step. Read this one most.
- [.claude/commands/implement-phase.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/.claude/commands/implement-phase.md) — the slash command that lands a phase. Delivery here is agent-driven and gated by `bin/check`.
- [.claude/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/.claude/README.md) — the whole workbench: subagents and commands.

**B — You are building a SaaS with Magik.** You are writing app code — models, screens, actions. **Nothing works yet**; the wiki is the target DSL, not a usable API.

- [wiki/Home.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Home.md) — the reference manual index.
- [wiki/Getting-Started.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Getting-Started.md) — the intended first run, end to end.
- [wiki/Models.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Models.md) · [wiki/Screens-And-Components.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Screens-And-Components.md) · [wiki/Actions.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Actions.md) — the three declarations most app code is made of.
- [wiki/Project-Layout.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Project-Layout.md) — where every file goes, and the filename ↔ declaration mapping in both directions. Read before writing a path.
- [wiki/Testing.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Testing.md) — the test DSL, inferred factories, the helpers, the parallel runner.
- [dummy/](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/dummy/README.md) — the invoicing/billing demo SaaS, following the canonical layout. Empty today.
- [docs/idea/09-app-scaffold.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/09-app-scaffold.md) — the AI harness `magik new` is meant to put in your app: `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt`, `.claude/agents` and `.claude/commands`, `docs/`, and which of them a regeneration may rewrite. The templates it describes: [lib/magik/cli/templates/app/](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/lib/magik/cli/templates/app/README.md). Whether `magik new` runs yet: `magik help --json`.

Both readers: [wiki/Error-Codes.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Error-Codes.md) and [wiki/Known-Gaps.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Known-Gaps.md).

## Resolve before you quote

- `gem list magik --remote --all`: what RubyGems actually serves. The published version is a name reservation; do not infer capability from it.
- `ruby -Ilib -e 'require "magik"; puts Magik::VERSION'`: what this checkout is stamped at.
- `ruby -Ilib -e 'require "magik"; puts Magik::SUBSYSTEMS.keys.inspect'`: every planned subsystem, from the map that drives autoloading. The authoritative list — not the copy in any document.
- `magik version --json` / `magik help --json`: the commands that run, and the registry of every command with its status, each marked `ready` or `planned`. **The authoritative answer to "what works".**
- `rake -T`: every task this checkout defines. What the repo can do, as opposed to what it plans to.
- `bin/check`: the gate — lint, tests, doc checks. Green means the change is landable.
- `bundle exec yard stats --list-undoc`: documentation coverage of what exists. Published at <https://developerz-ai.github.io/magik/api/>.

## Where do I look for X

- **What is Magik supposed to be**: [docs/idea/00-build-spec.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/00-build-spec.md). The source of truth: ten phases, thirteen build steps. Everything else elaborates on it.
- **Why the repo is arranged for an agent**: [docs/idea/07-ai-first.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/07-ai-first.md), then [.claude/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/.claude/README.md).
- **What actually works today**: `magik help --json`, then [wiki/Known-Gaps.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Known-Gaps.md). The answer is `version`, `help` and `docs`, and nothing else.
- **Where does this file go**: [wiki/Project-Layout.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Project-Layout.md) — one predictable mapping from filename to declaration, both directions, plus what each directory must not hold.
- **What shape does a declaration take**: [docs/idea/02-dsl-surface.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/02-dsl-surface.md) for the canonical form; the `wiki/` page for the reference version with a worked example.
- **Why is this a boot failure**: [docs/idea/03-guardrails.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/03-guardrails.md). The catalogue, each entry a boot failure by design — including the authorization, layout and upload refusals that came with architecture decision 13.
- **Can I replace a default**: [docs/idea/04-swap-points.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/04-swap-points.md) — DB, cache, jobs, search, realtime. Every swap needs a passing test on both sides before it is claimed. None exists yet.
- **Can I use my own components**: [docs/idea/08-component-overrides.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/08-component-overrides.md) for the reasoning; [wiki/Screens-And-Components.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Screens-And-Components.md) for the four-rung ladder, the kit contract and the resolution order.
- **What will it refuse to do**: [docs/idea/05-limits.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/05-limits.md). No offline, no heavy client-side compute, no SPA framework. Permanent, not a gap.
- **I hit a `MAGIK_*` code**: [wiki/Error-Codes.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Error-Codes.md). Run the `fix:` line verbatim — it is a command or an edit naming a file. Eight codes are raised by anything today — three `MAGIK_CLI_*`, four `MAGIK_DOCS_*`, and the root `MAGIK_ERROR` — and `ruby scripts/checks/error_codes.rb` re-derives that count rather than restating it. The rest are seeded from the guardrails and raised by nothing.
- **A CLI flag, a `--json` shape, an exit code**: [wiki/CLI-Reference.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/CLI-Reference.md).
- **Which module owns this**: [docs/architecture/01-module-map.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/01-module-map.md). **What may depend on what**: [docs/architecture/02-boundaries.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/02-boundaries.md).
- **How the tests are meant to run**: [docs/architecture/04-testing-strategy.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/04-testing-strategy.md) for the mechanism and its risks; [wiki/Testing.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Testing.md) for what you type.
- **Why is my change not reloading**: [wiki/Development-Loop.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Development-Loop.md), then [docs/architecture/08-dev-loop.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/08-dev-loop.md).
- **Where do secrets and env vars come from**: [docs/architecture/07-configuration-and-secrets.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/07-configuration-and-secrets.md).
- **How do I see what a running app is doing**: [docs/architecture/06-observability.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/06-observability.md).
- **How to run it in production**: [docs/ops/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/ops/README.md). Recommendations only.
- **The rules I must not break while editing this repo**: [CLAUDE.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/CLAUDE.md) and [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/AGENTS.md); the coding contract is [docs/architecture/00-conventions.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/00-conventions.md).
- **How to cut a release**: [PUBLISHING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/PUBLISHING.md), then [.claude/commands/release.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/.claude/commands/release.md).

## The agent workbench — .claude

Committed to the tree rather than kept in a local config, because the repo's way of working is part of the repo. A phase is landed by an agent running `/implement-phase` and gated by `bin/check`.

- [.claude/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/.claude/README.md): what is here and when to reach for it.

## The phases

Ten spec phases — 1, 2, 3, 4, 4b, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 — delivered in a thirteen-step build order that is deliberately **not** the same sequence: testing is spec Phase 9 and build step 5, so everything after it is test-driven; the API phase lands after auth/billing/admin because the admin panel is the first real consumer of the resource DSL. **Where the two orderings disagree, build order wins.** The table below is numbered by phase identity and ordered by delivery. Definitions of "done" and version milestones: [ROADMAP.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/ROADMAP.md). **All ten are planned. None is built.**

| Phase | Built at | Ships | Reference page |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Foundation | steps 1–2 | `App.define`, `model`, `migrate`, `:money`/`:file`/`:duration`, `computed`, UUIDv7, tenant injection, the option tables, `magik new/generate/console/server/describe` | [wiki/Models.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Models.md) · [wiki/CLI-Reference.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/CLI-Reference.md) |
| 2 Rendering & actions | steps 3–4 | `component`, `screen`, `action`, **`policy`**, **`layout`**, the kit, theming, router, hot reload | [wiki/Screens-And-Components.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Screens-And-Components.md) · [wiki/Actions.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Actions.md) |
| 9 Testing | step 5 | the `test` DSL, inferred factories, the helpers, the parallel runner — early, so everything after it is TDD'd | [wiki/Testing.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Testing.md) |
| 3 Realtime | step 6 | `live`, `channel`, `broadcast`, `presence` — opt-in per screen | [wiki/Realtime.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Realtime.md) |
| 4 Jobs | step 7 | `job`, `retries times:`, schedules, the transactional queue, `magik worker` | [wiki/Jobs.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Jobs.md) |
| 4b Media | step 8 | `attachment`, direct-to-storage upload, magic-byte sniffing, derivatives, signed delivery, a wrapped video seam. No wiki page yet | [docs/idea/06-phases.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/06-phases.md) |
| 5 Money & compliance | step 9 | `ledger`, `audited`, `immutable_after:`, `idempotent_by`, `flow` | [wiki/Money-And-Ledgers.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Money-And-Ledgers.md) |
| 7 Auth, billing, admin | step 10 | `auth`, `billing`, `admin_panel` (a `policy:` is required), `tenant_by`, teams and seats | [wiki/Auth-Billing-Admin.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Auth-Billing-Admin.md) |
| 6 API & integration | step 11 | `api`, `resource`, incoming and outgoing `webhook`, API auth, rate limits | [wiki/API-And-Webhooks.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/API-And-Webhooks.md) |
| 8 i18n, PWA, notifications | step 12 | `locales`, `translatable:`, `pwa`, `notification`, email production | [wiki/Home.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Home.md) |
| + Domains (spec item 12, not a phase) | step 13 | `domain`, boot-time boundary enforcement, `magik check --scale` | [wiki/Domains.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Domains.md) |

## The guardrails

The product **is** the enforcement. Declarations are refused at boot rather than at runtime, each refusal carrying a code, a cause and a runnable `fix:` — which is the correction signal an agent acts on. Full reasoning: [docs/idea/03-guardrails.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/03-guardrails.md). Full catalogue: [wiki/Error-Codes.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Error-Codes.md).

- Ledger entries must balance — `MAGIK_LEDGER_UNBALANCED`
- No PAN-shaped field may exist — `MAGIK_MODEL_FORBIDDEN_FIELD`
- No cross-domain direct model access — `MAGIK_DOMAIN_BOUNDARY`
- No in-process state across requests in a screen or action — `MAGIK_RENDER_SCREEN_STATEFUL`
- No timestamp rendered without an explicit timezone — `MAGIK_RENDER_TIMESTAMP_NO_ZONE`
- No query without `tenant_id` in its `WHERE` — `MAGIK_SCALE_UNSCOPED_QUERY`, via `magik check --scale`
- **No surface reaches a model without naming a policy verb** — `MAGIK_POLICY_UNDECLARED`, the load-bearing one: it makes authorization non-optional the way `tenant_id` is, and makes an unprotected admin panel a boot failure rather than a documented risk. Its siblings refuse a predicate that does I/O, an unknown verb, a missing `default :deny`, and a rule that passes on a `nil` record
- **No screen without a layout**, and no `nav_item` naming a screen that does not exist — `MAGIK_LAYOUT_MISSING` · `MAGIK_LAYOUT_UNKNOWN_SCREEN`
- **No unbounded upload** — a `:file` field or an `attachment` with no `max_size` and no `content_types` — `MAGIK_MODEL_UNCONSTRAINED_UPLOAD`

Rendered shape, identical in the terminal, the development error page and `--json` — it is one object, `Magik::Error#to_h`:

```text
MAGIK_LEDGER_UNBALANCED: entry :invoice_issued debits 14999, credits 14900
  fix: correct the amounts in app/ledgers/receivables.rb — debits must equal credits
```

Eight codes exist today: the root `MAGIK_ERROR`, the CLI's `MAGIK_CLI_UNKNOWN_COMMAND`, `MAGIK_CLI_COMMAND_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and `MAGIK_CLI_INVALID_OPTION`, and the four `MAGIK_DOCS_*` behind `magik docs`. Resolve the list rather than quoting it: `ruby scripts/checks/error_codes.rb` prints the count, and `jq -r '.error_codes[].code' magik.manifest.json` prints the names. A bare grep for the prefix over `lib/` over-counts — it also matches the `MAGIK_DOCS_ROOT` environment variable and the codes named in doc-comment examples. Every other code on the catalogue page is seeded from the guardrails and raised by nothing.

`MAGIK_` is a prefix, not a promise that a string is a code. Two other things wear it: environment variables (`MAGIK_DOCS_ROOT`, `MAGIK_YARD_MIN_COVERAGE`), and every `MAGIK_DEV_*` code, which is repo-internal — the refusals `bin/` prints and the findings `scripts/checks/` emits, both of which ship to nobody and are in no catalogue. That is the whole rule: a `MAGIK_` code is a **framework** code whose token comes from the closed set and which an app author can hit, or it is `MAGIK_DEV_*` and belongs to this repository alone ([docs/architecture/03-error-codes.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/03-error-codes.md)).

## The limits

Permanent exclusions, not gaps. They are refusals with codes rather than silent no-ops, because a limit that fails quietly is worse than one that refuses loudly. Full detail: [docs/idea/05-limits.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/05-limits.md).

- **No offline support.** The server is the single source of truth — `MAGIK_PWA_OFFLINE_UNSUPPORTED`.
- **No heavy client-side compute.** Canvas editors, games, in-browser media editing — `MAGIK_RENDER_CLIENT_COMPUTE_UNSUPPORTED`.
- **No SPA framework, ever.** React/Vue/Svelte owning rendering is forbidden; attaching your own JavaScript behaviour to server-rendered markup is not.
- **No GraphQL.** REST, generated from `resource` declarations. A second query language is a second authorization surface.
- **CRuby is not the target.** TruffleRuby is production; CRuby `>= 3.2` is for tooling. Where they diverge, TruffleRuby is documented behaviour.
- **Not a multi-gem monorepo.** One gem, subsystem modules under `lib/magik/`. Extraction stays possible; it is not promised.

## The file map

### Design — docs/idea

- [00-build-spec.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/00-build-spec.md): the specification. Source of truth — thirteen non-negotiable decisions, ten phases, thirteen build steps.
- [01-thesis.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/01-thesis.md): why this framework exists, and the axioms everything else follows.
- [02-dsl-surface.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/02-dsl-surface.md): the canonical shape of every declaration. One grammar.
- [03-guardrails.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/03-guardrails.md): what fails at boot, and why boot rather than runtime.
- [04-swap-points.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/04-swap-points.md): every opinionated default and its escape hatch — including the component override ladder.
- [05-limits.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/05-limits.md): what Magik refuses to do, permanently.
- [06-phases.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/06-phases.md): the ten phases in detail, the thirteen-step build order they are delivered in, and the definition of done per phase.
- [07-ai-first.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/07-ai-first.md): the primary developer is an agent, and what follows from that.
- [08-component-overrides.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/08-component-overrides.md): the component kit is a default too — four rungs, a contract, a resolution order.
- [09-app-scaffold.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/09-app-scaffold.md): the app scaffold — three stages, what each emits, and who owns each generated file.
- [10-saas-coverage.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/10-saas-coverage.md): the adversarial audit of the 99% claim, and the command that re-counts the table. It is where `policy`, `layout` and media came from.
- [11-dsl-as-tool-surface.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/11-dsl-as-tool-surface.md): the DSL as a tool surface — the rules new grammar is designed against, why `magik describe` exists, and why `magik mcp` is deferred.
- [12-the-range.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/12-the-range.md): the two axes one framework has to span, from a weekend idea to a large product.
- [13-decisions.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/idea/13-decisions.md): the governance model — the agent decides within the spec's frame, what is reserved to the owner, what a decision owes, and the log of decisions taken.

### Internals — docs/architecture

- [00-conventions.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/00-conventions.md): file layout, naming, export surface — the coding contract.
- [01-module-map.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/01-module-map.md): twenty-one subsystems, one reason to change each. Re-derive with `ruby -Ilib -e 'require "magik"; puts Magik::SUBSYSTEMS.keys.join(" ")'`.
- [02-boundaries.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/02-boundaries.md): what may depend on what. A violation is a failure, not a review comment.
- [03-error-codes.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/03-error-codes.md): how a code is declared, owned and kept unique.
- [04-testing-strategy.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/04-testing-strategy.md): thread-parallel workers, template-database cloning, and the honest risks.
- [05-adding-a-feature.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/05-adding-a-feature.md): the end-to-end loop with a command per step.
- [06-observability.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/06-observability.md): what a running app emits, and what it does not.
- [07-configuration-and-secrets.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/07-configuration-and-secrets.md): where config comes from, and how a secret reaches a process.
- [08-dev-loop.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/08-dev-loop.md): how hot reload works, and what it cannot reload.
- [09-shipped-docs.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/09-shipped-docs.md): why the gem carries its own manual, and what `magik docs` serves.
- [10-performance-defaults.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/10-performance-defaults.md): the defaults that cost something at runtime, and the seams they sit behind.
- [11-jobs-backend.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/11-jobs-backend.md): which Postgres queue is wrapped, by what locking mechanism, and where it stops being the right answer.
- [12-runtime-verification.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/architecture/12-runtime-verification.md): the runtime measurements decisions 1 and 2 rest on. Re-derive with `ruby scripts/probes/runtime.rb --json`; never quote a number from it.

### Operations — docs/ops

- [Operations index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/docs/ops/README.md): running a Magik app for real. Recommendations only; the framework depends on none of it.

### The reference manual — wiki

The public documentation surface. Source of truth is `wiki/` in this repository, browsable at <https://github.com/developerz-ai/magik/wiki>. Every page carries a `Status:` line and documents **intended** behaviour.

- [Home](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Home.md): the index, with a reading path per audience.
- [Installation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Installation.md): TruffleRuby as the production target, CRuby 3.2+ for tooling, and what `gem install magik` actually gives you today.
- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Getting-Started.md): the intended first run — `magik new` → `bin/setup` → `magik server`.
- [Development loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Development-Loop.md): hot reload, the console, generators, `--watch`, the error page. No JS build step, ever.
- [Project layout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Project-Layout.md): the annotated tree, the filename ↔ declaration mapping both directions, how it scales to domains, and generated versus hand-written.
- [CLI reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/CLI-Reference.md): every command, flag, `--json` shape and exit code, with the ones that run today marked. `magik help --json` is the authority on which those are.
- [Models](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Models.md): `model`, `migrate`, field types, tenancy, UUIDv7, the Sequel seam.
- [Screens and components](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Screens-And-Components.md): `screen`, `component`, the kit, theming, and the four-rung override ladder for your own components.
- [Actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Actions.md): the only thing that mutates. Params, guards, routing by convention, idempotency.
- [Realtime](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Realtime.md): `live`, `channel`, `broadcast`, `presence` — opt-in per screen, and free when undeclared.
- [Jobs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Jobs.md): the only thing that runs async. The transactional queue, retries, schedules.
- [Money and ledgers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Money-And-Ledgers.md): integer cents, double-entry, audit, immutability, idempotency, flows.
- [API and webhooks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/API-And-Webhooks.md): `api`, `resource`, incoming and outgoing webhooks, API auth, plan-based rate limits.
- [Auth, billing, admin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Auth-Billing-Admin.md): Rodauth-backed auth, Stripe billing, generated admin panels, `tenant_by`.
- [Testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Testing.md): the `test` DSL over Minitest, every helper in use, inferred factories, generated tests, all cores by default.
- [Domains](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Domains.md): `depends_on`, `exposes`, `publishes_events`, and boot-time boundary enforcement.
- [Error codes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Error-Codes.md): the format contract, the codes that are live today, and the catalogue seeded from the guardrails. Which rows are live is re-derived by `ruby scripts/checks/error_codes.rb`, never counted by hand.
- [Known gaps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Known-Gaps.md): the honest page. The gap is the entire framework.
- [FAQ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/FAQ.md): why TruffleRuby, why Sequel, why Minitest, why htmx, why no offline, is it production ready, how it differs from Rails.
- [Contributing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/wiki/Contributing.md): a pointer to the root guide.

- [lib/magik.rb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/lib/magik.rb): the module — `VERSION`, `Error`, `SUBSYSTEMS`, and the autoload map. The authoritative subsystem list.
- [lib/magik/version.rb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/developerz-ai/magik/main/lib/magik/version.rb): the version constant, documented as a name reservation.
